title: Linear Regression & Classification
description: Explore mathematical foundations: line fitting with Mean Squared Error (MSE) and binary classification with Logistic Regression.

slides.title: Fitting Lines: Linear Regression 📈
slides.content:
# Linear Regression

Linear regression models the relationship between dependent scalar $y$ and explanatory variables $X$:

$$
\hat{y} = w \cdot x + b
$$

* **$w$ (Weight/Slope):** Multiplier determining the sensitivity of $y$ to $x$.
* **$b$ (Bias/Intercept):** Baseline value when $x = 0$.

### The Cost Function: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
To measure error across $N$ training points:

$$
MSE = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2
$$

Squaring the errors penalizes large deviations severely and guarantees a smooth, convex parabola with a single global minimum!

slides.title: Classification with Logistic Regression 🎯
slides.content:
# Logistic Regression & The Sigmoid Function

When target $y \in \{0, 1\}$, a straight line can predict outputs less than 0 or greater than 1, violating probability axioms.

To squash linear outputs into valid probabilities $(0, 1)$, we pass $z = w \cdot x + b$ through the **Sigmoid (logistic) function**:

$$
\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}
$$

* When $z = 0$, $\sigma(z) = 0.5$.
* When $z \to +\infty$, $\sigma(z) \to 1.0$.
* When $z \to -\infty$, $\sigma(z) \to 0.0$.

quizData.question: What is the exact output of the Sigmoid function $\sigma(z)$ when the linear input $z = 0$?
quizData.explanation: When z = 0, e^(-0) = 1, giving 1 / (1 + 1) = 0.5, representing the decision boundary cutoff.
